\chapter{Counting Subarrays, Pairs \& Triples: the Contribution Technique}
\label{ch:contribution}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{There are $\bigO{n^2}$ subarrays and $\bigO{n^2}$ pairs, but the answer only needs how much each element contributes.}}
\end{tcolorbox}

\chapterfacts{1500}{2400}{7}{14}{30}

\begin{plannedbox}[Planned Contents --- this chapter is not written yet]
\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item Counting subarrays: fix the right end, fix the left end, complementary counting
    \item Contribution of an element: in how many subarrays (or pairs) does it count, and with what weight
    \item Sum over all pairs: sorting and prefix sums for $\sum |a_i - a_j|$ and similar
    \item Fix the middle element: left counts times right counts; triples and the cost of each extra dimension
    \item Pairs with an index condition and a value condition; small values: frequency arrays and convolutions
    \item Contribution with nearest smaller/greater indices (computing them is the stack-queue-heap book; per-bit sums are Chapter~\ref{ch:bitwise})
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Part B --- Patterns} (with candidate problems, checked when the chapter is written)

    \item \textbf{Small-value counting}
